analyst_view.overall: Early view: Palace may have a new manager by then, as Pierre Sage's job was reported to be under threat with the club bottom of the Premier League; Adam Wharton and Yeremy Pino should be back after serving their bans against Real Sociedad. Jagiellonia (29th, 3 points) have lost three of four, so this home game in Bialystok could be close to must-win for them.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean higher: Palace's European games have averaged almost four goals (4-0, 2-3, 2-2, 1-1), and Jagiellonia's have averaged nearly three. Palace's set-piece defending has been a weak point all autumn, and Jagiellonia scored three at home to Ararat, so both sides should score.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Palace should have more of the ball and a desperate home side will throw men forward, which roughly matches the site's split.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean higher: Palace have had two players sent off in recent weeks and picked up several bookings against Hoffenheim, and a Jagiellonia side facing elimination is likely to make it physical in December conditions.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. Jagiellonia failed to score in their defeats to Anderlecht and Levski, while Palace's line-up depends on their manager situation and league schedule, so I stay with the number for now.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Nothing yet points strongly either way; this will move with Palace's team news and whoever is picking it.
